text: The kappa architecture — solving lambda's real cost by refusing to have two codepaths in the first place.

Lambda maintains speed layer code and batch layer code, two implementations of the same aggregation. Kappa uses one streaming pipeline for both live processing and historical reprocessing, by replaying old events.
That only works if the source can actually be replayed — enough retention to go back far enough, or raw events durably stored somewhere replayable. Without that, there's nothing to replay.
Kappa is usually preferred when available, since it avoids lambda's drift risk entirely. Next up: data modeling at scale — from processing model to data model.
